newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes higher on flood watch, funds.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes higher on flood watch, funds.

text.p: Fund buying, centered in new crop July, helped boost CBOT wheat futures to a higher close as did other speculative positioning on the potential for flooding this spring in portions of the U.S. Midwest, traders said.
Fundamentals were little changed with wet weather in parts of the U.S. Midwest cited as potentially supportive in wheat futures. There were forecasts for floods.
"That hasn't happened yet but it might. That should help Minneapolis but it's not fresh news," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter.
The U.S. Commerce Department on Tuesday forecast the most widespread spring flooding in the U.S. in a decade.
The U.S. upper Midwest/Plains spring wheat growing region was under the greatest threat of flooding but MGE spring wheat futures contracts were only mildly higher at the close.
Some traders said the ability of soybeans to recover also boosted wheat futures.
"Rosenthal came in and bought a couple million more. It's just technical and following beans," a trader said. Others said Rosenthal Collins bought at least five million bushels of July.
CBOT wheat closed 4-1/4 cents higher to one lower, with March up 3/4 at $3.77 and May up 2-3/4 at $3.83-3/4.

Traders said the open interest in the March contract at roughly 860,000 bushels early Tuesday indicated little concern about expiration of that contract. The CBOT March contracts were slated to expire at 1201 CST Wednesday.
Technicians early Tuesday cited first support in the May at $3.77-1/4 and second support at $3.67-1/4. The session low for May was $3.79.
First resistance in the May was noted at $3.87-1/4 and second resistance was at $3.97-1/4. The session high for May was $3.85.
The four- and 20-day moving averages were giving off bullish signals early Tuesday.
The nine-day relative strength index (RSI) in the May closed at 61.4 percent. The market generally considers an RSI of 70 or more as overbought and 30 or less as oversold.

In addition to the Rosenthal Collins' purchase of five million bushels of July, Merrill Lynch Futures bought two million July and Cargill Investor Services bought 1.5 million bushels of July, traders said. Cargill Inc sold 2.5 million July, they said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 14,000 contracts, below the 15,970 traded Monday.
In wheat options, Cargill Investor Services sold 100 May $3.80 calls and sold 100 May $3.80 puts at 24-1/2 cents and Refco Inc bought 100 July $3.60 puts at 13-1/8 to 13-1/4 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 2,500 contracts, below the 5,909 traded Monday.
